Source: World Bank International Debt Statistics (IDS) (2026), via the Development Finance Observatory; latest period 2022.

Steps: The World Bank publishes IDS as six bulk files, split by debtor name. All six are downloaded each time the pipeline runs, and replace the previous copy, so the data reflects the World Bank's latest release. Non-debt statistics are excluded, including population, balance of payments, investment and reserves. GNI is kept, because some debt ratios are shares of it. Exports of goods, services and primary income, and the three debt ratios that are shares of it, are excluded until the ontology can describe them. Debt forgiveness grants, the stock-flow reconciliation residual, the annual changes in debt stocks and interest arrears, and the present value of debt are also excluded. IDS reports a value for every debtor, creditor and series, including pairs with no lending between them, so most figures are zero. Zeros are kept on world totals, and within or after a period of lending between a debtor and a creditor. They are omitted where a creditor has not lent to a debtor, for the years before lending began, and for averages in years with no new commitments, since there is nothing to average. Debtor and creditor codes are standardised to Data Commons IDs used across the platform, so data can be compared across datasets. Where a series names a single lender in its code, such as debt owed to the IBRD, that lender becomes the creditor. Every figure is reported against the year, the debtor and the creditor, and the dimensions the World Bank encodes in each series code, such as type of flow, maturity and creditor type. GNI is the exception: it describes the debtor economy, so it is reported against the year and the economy alone. Ratios record what they are a share of: GNI or total external debt stocks. Every amount is reported in US dollars at current prices. 1 more step not shown.
